state.label: El Niño Advisory · Strengthening
state.detail: El Niño conditions are present and strengthening fast. NOAA is at a full El Niño Advisory, with an 81% chance of a very strong event in Oct–Dec and a 97% chance it persists into early spring 2027.

narrative: El Niño is now present and strengthening fast — the sustainability question that dominated the spring has largely resolved. NOAA moved to a full El Niño Advisory, and the weekly Niño 3.4 index reached +1.7°C by mid-June, up sharply from +0.5°C in late May. NOAA now puts an 81% chance of a very strong El Niño during October–December that would rank among the largest events since 1950, with a 97% chance the event persists through early spring 2027. Atmospheric coupling has established: thunderstorm activity has shifted to the central and eastern Pacific and is suppressed over Indonesia. The model ensemble has trended warmer month-on-month — GFDL's July run has all 30 members peaking at least competitive with the strongest events of the past century, and ECMWF flags the possibility of anomalies above +3°C by autumn. The event is no longer 'developing' as a question; it is developing in force. The remaining uncertainty is the magnitude of the peak (strong vs very strong vs record) and the exact timing of the autumn–winter maximum.
